title: Post a small parcel fully through a gate's spring-flap mail slot, where the hand cannot follow it in
instruction: Post the white parcel through the mail slot.
context: Pushing a small parcel through a sprung mail-slot flap, at a door or a gate, is an everyday act most adults know. One left halfway in is easily taken or soaked and holds the flap open. Unlike placing an item through an open mailbox door (BEHAVIOR-1K's sending_packages, mailing_letters), the slot plate stops the hand, so where the parcel is held decides whether it drops into the box or stays stuck in the slot.
setup: 'In front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, the midline is halfway between the arm bases. Gate section (fixed): three 140 x 19 mm cedar boards side by side, 420 mm wide (9 cm right to 33 cm left of the midline), 264 mm tall with a 19 x 19 mm cap rail, standing across the table; its outer face 36.3 cm in front of the bases. Mail slot through it: a Salsbury 4045 magazine-size slot, solid brass. Face plate 330 x 89 x 3 mm on the outer face (outer face 36.0 cm in front of the bases), four screws; opening 286 mm wide (centred 12 cm left of the midline), floor 140 mm and ceiling 202 mm up; rough opening in the boards 286 x 64 mm. Flap: 0.8 mm brass leaf 283 x 60 mm with a 3 mm rolled lower edge, on two pins at its top corners 200.5 mm up, hanging in the opening; 130 g; swings inward up to 83 degrees; closed mainly by its weight (about 0.036 N m when 70 degrees open) and a light spring of 0.005 N m per rad, damping 0.005 N m s per rad. Catch box behind the gate (grey painted 2 mm sheet steel): 220 mm deep inside (38.2 to 60.2 cm), 364 mm wide inside, roof underside 262 mm up, a floor sheet, a rear door with a round cam lock, and a fixed 2 mm steel anti-fishing drop chute (as in through-wall drop boxes) 120 mm long across its width, sloping down 35 degrees from the lower inner edge of the slot (139 mm up, 38.2 cm from the bases); the only way in is the slot. Parcel (loose): a white corrugated crush-proof mailer box, 6 x 2-1/2 x 1 in inside, 162 x 76 x 32 mm outside, packed to 150 g, lying flat on the table, long side front to back, centred 21.9 cm in front of the bases and 12 cm left of the midline (its far end 60 mm short of the plate), its taped tuck end toward the slot, shipping label up. Friction, static / sliding: parcel 0.4 / 0.3; gate, plate, flap and box 0.3 / 0.25. A black house-number plaque is on the gate right of the slot. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Score 1.0: the whole parcel is inside the catch box (no part of it in the slot or in front of the gate's inner face, 38.2 cm from the bases), it is at rest, the flap is shut (its lower edge no more than 5 mm inside its hanging position) and no gripper or finger surface is within 5 mm of the parcel. Score 0 for everything else: the parcel on the table or anywhere outside the box, stuck in the slot (flat or tilted, partly outside), on top of the box, inside with the flap more than 5 mm open, still moving, or still touched or held. The trial ends at 1.0 once the 1.0 condition has held for 1 s; otherwise it scores the state at the last step.
reset_notes: 1. Open the catch box's rear door and take the parcel out; shut the door. 2. Lay the parcel flat, label up, taped end toward the slot, centred 21.9 cm in front of the arm bases and 12 cm left of the midline (far end 60 mm short of the plate). 3. Check that the flap hangs shut. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate. Rigid parts. Slot plate and flap sizes are Salsbury 4045's; leaf and plate thickness, flap mass (brass at those sizes) and spring are estimates. Parcel: a real 6x2.5x1 in crush-proof mailer, about 26-40 g empty (listed bundle weights); outside size is inside plus board, packed to 150 g, centred; rigid, as a packed mailer box barely flexes. The fixed chute is simulated as a hinge held on its stop. Friction typical of cardboard on painted steel and brass, not measured.
